title: Concatenating DNFs evaluates as their disjunction
statement: Let $\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k$ be DNF formulas over $n$ variables, and let $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ be a Boolean assignment. Form the single DNF whose term-list is the concatenation of the term-lists of $\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k$. Then this concatenated formula evaluates to true at $x$ if and only if at least one of the formulas $\varphi_i$ evaluates to true at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: a finite list of DNF formulas over n variables
a Boolean assignment x on n variables
replaced:
For any input $x$, the value of the concatenated DNF at $x$ equals the disjunction over
all $\varphi$ in the list of $\varphi.\mathrm{eval}\,x$; that is, it holds iff some
component DNF holds at $x$.
